elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 2.1 now reads in full: "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment." This replaces the prior three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay and is reinforced by retained Section 12.3 ("Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."). No other rendered clause imposes a volume cap or shortfall charge on Customer; Section 7.1 expressly bars unidentified "minimum-use" charges.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.1: "Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form... unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify." The defined term "Fees" is limited to amounts "payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services," so payment obligations run only to ordered Services or usage-based pricing. No edit needed.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: it presupposes a surviving purchase commitment. After the edit no commitment exists at all (Section 2.1 as rendered negates any minimum purchase or volume obligation), so the condition does not apply and the customer-protective outcome is strictly better than a 12-month-limited commitment.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Conditional on there being a commitment to reduce. The offending "without reduction or termination rights" language was deleted with the commitment itself, so there is nothing left to reduce; the fallback mechanic is unnecessary rather than omitted.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Conditional on a shortfall mechanic existing. No rendered clause imposes a shortfall or take-or-pay penalty on Customer (the Section 22.2/22.3 shortfall references concern Vendor underpayment audits), so no true-up substitution is required.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty. (independent check of retained formulas)
elements.evidence: No retained instalment, liquidated-damages, or contingent make-whole formula survives in the rendered text; Section 7.1 permits only Fees identified in an Order Form and prohibits unidentified minimum-use charges.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single-sentence replacement of Section 2.1 delivers the express no-minimum-purchase-or-volume statement, and the second preferred element was already met by unedited Section 7.1 read with the defined term "Fees" (amounts payable under an Order Form).

The edit is minimal: exactly one operative sentence was replaced, the drafter added no survival tail, no procedure, no damages language, and no requirement outside the MINCOMMIT checklist. Customer-favourable retained language (Section 7.1's bar on unidentified minimum-use charges; Section 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement) was preserved rather than restated, so there is no duplicated operative term.

Intent is preserved and an internal contradiction is cured: the deleted take-or-pay directly conflicted with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no minimum-volume commitment. Pricing, Order Form mechanics, term, and audit provisions are untouched, and the edit leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference in the cited text.

Fallback elements are recorded as vacuously met because each is conditional on a surviving commitment or shortfall mechanic; none survives. Verify separately that no Order Form, exhibit, or termination-for-convenience clause elsewhere cross-references the deleted "Section 2.1 commitment" (e.g., a fee-schedule discount premised on the USD 2,000,000 volume) — if such a reference exists it must be conformed, otherwise the edit would leave a dangling cross-reference.

No severity escalation is warranted; the original clause was walk-away territory (multi-year take-or-pay expressly "without reduction or termination rights"), and the proposed language resolves it at the preferred position, with the fallback correctly offered in the margin comment rather than drafted into the operative text.
